newsitem.title: UK: Britain to press for prompt truckers compensation.
newsitem.headline: Britain to press for prompt truckers compensation.

text.p: Britain's transport minister pledged on Saturday to ensure prompt settlement of compensation claims by British truckers hit by a crippling 12-day French lorry drivers' strike.

Sir George Young said he had received assurances from France that compensation claims would be processed speedily and told BBC radio he wanted to see British drivers and firms receiving payments within a matter of months.

"The damage is serious. There is no reason why British haulage firms should have their viability, their very existence, threatened by illegal action in France. Compensation is payable and I am going to make sure it is paid," Young said.
"Until the money changes hands, until the firms that have suffered serious damage actually get compensated, I will continue to take a personal interest in this," he added.

About 1,000 British drivers were affected by the French strike over pay and conditions. It was not clear how much money British firms planned to claim in compensation for loss of earnings, damage to vehicles or deterioration of cargoes.
One haulier said he was forming an action group in a bid to sue the French government en masse.

"We have had a lot of inquiries so far. Probably between 30 and 40 people are already signed up. I think the more we get, the more punch we are going to have against the French government," said Peter Davis, managing director of the haulage firm Davex Ltd.

British drivers have bitter memories of a similar French truckers' dispute in 1992 when claims for compensation hit difficulties in obtaining supporting statements from French police and other authorities.
Young said delays of two-and-a-half years or more by the French authorities in settling claims after the 1992 strike were "unacceptable".
European Union Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock said the European Commission would tackle concern over the speed with which compensation would be agreed.

"The Commission has also been appraised by road haulage associations from throughout the Community, expressing concern at the rapidity with which requests for compensation will be processed," Kinnock told BBC radio.
"The Commission will take up this matter with the French authorities," he said.
